source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension, in collaboration with the Siem Reap Provincial Department of Agriculture and an economic development program, trifold brochure "វិធីដាំខ្នុរ" (How to Plant Jackfruit) / "បទពិសោធន៍ជោគជ័យ ក្នុងការដាំខ្នុរ របស់កសិករគំរូ" (Successful Experience in Growing Jackfruit of a Model Farmer), Siem Reap, 2013
text:
A planting pit should be dug with a square/round cross-section and a certain depth (the brochure diagram and the accompanying text give conflicting digits for the exact pit width and depth in spans, so the precise figure is not reported here — see summary notes).

The pit should be layered while being refilled: alternating a layer of organic material (a mix of topsoil, chopped banana stem, rice straw or husk, wood ash, and cow or chicken manure) with a layer of plain topsoil, repeating this layering until the pit is filled level with the ground surface at the pit's rim.

The spacing between one planting pit and the next should be about 8 meters.

After being prepared and filled in this way, the pit should be left to rest for 2 to 3 weeks before a seedling is planted in it.
